events.title: Joan of Arc Lifts the Siege of Orléans
events.description: Led by the teenage Joan of Arc, French forces broke the English siege of Orléans after days of fierce assaults on the English strongholds around the city.
events.significance: The victory turned the tide of the Hundred Years' War and set Charles VII on the road to his coronation at Reims.

events.title: Birth of Miguel Hidalgo
events.description: Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla, the Mexican priest who later raised the 'Grito de Dolores', was born in 1753.
events.significance: Hidalgo is honored as the father of Mexican independence, because his 1810 uprising began the country's long struggle to break free from Spanish rule.

events.title: Coca-Cola Is First Served
events.description: In Atlanta, Georgia, pharmacist John Pemberton's new syrup was mixed with carbonated water and sold at Jacobs' Pharmacy. Pemberton had developed it as a tonic, and it became a soda-fountain drink.
events.significance: It was the start of one of the world's best-known brands and a symbol of global consumer culture.

events.title: Victory in Europe Day
events.description: Germany's unconditional surrender took effect, ending the Second World War in Europe. Crowds celebrated in London, Paris, New York and many other cities.
events.significance: The day marked the end of Nazi Germany and of nearly six years of war in Europe, and it is still commemorated each year.

events.title: Smallpox Declared Eradicated
events.description: The World Health Assembly formally declared the world free of smallpox, following a worldwide vaccination and surveillance campaign.
events.significance: Smallpox remains the only human infectious disease ever eradicated. It had killed hundreds of millions of people over the centuries.
